The  story  of  the  buccaneers  in  Jamaica  is  true  and  is  tied  to  Hemy  Morgan. 
Numerous  ships  would  stop  in  Jamaica  before  returning  to  Europe.  Buccaneers  would 
sell  large  quantities  of  beef  to  ships  who  needed  a  food  supply  for  the  long  return  voyage. 
This  buccaneer  business  of  selling  beef  was  beginning  to  cut  into  Spanish  trade.

made,  not  without  a  great  amount  of  quarrelling  as  was  to

and sailor. Use of the surname Morgan has been extremely common throughout the history of 
Wales. The 1811 census of England and Wales found that more than 25% of Welsh property 
owners went by Morgan or derivatives (Morgen, Morgane, Morghan, Morghann, Morghyn).
